LESSON: DEVELOPMENTS IN MEDIUM OF TRADE

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: People and Relationship s
Topic 2.4: Developments in Medium of trade

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Developments in Medium of trade. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How has money transformed trade in Africa?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. compare barter trade and the use of currency trade in Africa
2. trace the factors that led to the introduction of money in Africa
3. appreciate the medium of trade for sustainability

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: DEVELOPMENTS IN MEDIUM OF TRADE
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Developments in Medium of trade helps you succeed in SOCIAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: DEVELOPMENTS IN MEDIUM OF TRADE
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Compare barter trade and the use of currency trade in Africa

What this means
In this part you learn to compare barter trade and the use of currency trade in Africa. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: compare barter trade and the use of currency trade in Africa.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Developments in Medium of trade” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can compare barter trade and the use of currency trade in Africa. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Trace the factors that led to the introduction of money in Africa

What this means
In this part you learn to trace the factors that led to the introduction of money in Africa. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: trace the factors that led to the introduction of money in Africa.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to Developments in Medium of trade.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can trace the factors that led to the introduction of money in Africa. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the medium of trade for sustainability

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the medium of trade for sustainability. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the medium of trade for sustainability.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Participate: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the medium of trade for sustainability. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Developments in Medium of trade is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “Developments in Medium of trade” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: compare barter trade and the use of currency trade in Africa)

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to Developments in Medium of trade. (skill: trace the factors that led to the introduction of money in Africa)

Example 3: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take. (skill: appreciate the medium of trade for sustainability)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Developments in Medium of trade to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: compare barter trade and the use of currency trade in Africa.
3. Practise this skill: trace the factors that led to the introduction of money in Africa.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the medium of trade for sustainability.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Developments in Medium of trade from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Developments in Medium of trade: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Developments in Medium of trade?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How has money transformed trade in Africa?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Developments in Medium of trade means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: compare barter trade and the use of currency trade in Africa.
5. Be able to: trace the factors that led to the introduction of money in Africa.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
